Headstart 20x
open source
GitHub Crosswalk 20x FedRAMP 2026 rules mycroft.io

How far is your ISO 27001 or SOC 2 program from FedRAMP 20x?

Headstart 20x reads your Statement of Applicability or SOC 2 report and lays it against the 46 Key Security Indicators and the FedRAMP rules for Class B, C or D. It shows where your program gives you a head start, where it falls short, and what 20x adds. Your files stay in your browser.

Start from what you already hold

An ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Statement of Applicability or a SOC 2 report. Headstart reads it against the 46 Key Security Indicators and the FedRAMP rules for the class you choose.

Excel or CSV. Headstart looks for the Annex A control IDs (A.5.1 to A.8.34), whether each is applicable, and its implementation status if you track one.

Or paste rows from your SoA
Drop the report PDF and let the scanner fill the form

The text is read in your browser. The scanner finds the report type, period, categories in scope and every test result in Section 4, and shows what it found for you to confirm. Nothing is uploaded.

Key Security Indicators

Built and maintained by Mycroft and released as open source under Apache-2.0 on GitHub. Not a FedRAMP tool and not endorsed by FedRAMP. The mappings are Mycroft's own work and are open to review. The page makes no network requests unless you choose the on-device Gemma step, which downloads the model once.

Key Security Indicators and FedRAMP rules from FedRAMP's Consolidated Rules for 2026, version . ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control titles and AICPA Trust Services Criteria identifiers are used for identification; the standards themselves are published by ISO and the AICPA. PDF text is read with pdf.js (Apache-2.0). Optional on-device reading is powered by Gemma 4 (Google), under the Gemma Terms of Use, running through WebGPU kernels by the Hugging Face webml community; it downloads the model once and only when you ask.
